_about: Plautus and Terence in English, translator per title. Plautus: Henry T. Riley's prose Comedies (Bohn, 1852; 1913 printing, 2 vols., raw IA, complete) and his Captivi and Mostellaria (clean Gutenberg). Terence: Riley's prose Comedies (Bohn) and George Colman's verse, clean Gutenberg; W. R. Goodluck's Andrian. Paul Nixon's Loeb Plautus vol. 1 (1916; Gutenberg, Latin facing kept) added 2026-10-02 from the bilingual catalogue. Latin-facing Loebs of 1930 or earlier added 2026-10-02 as raw IA OCR (translator per row); the scan's printing was checked for a post-1930 revision notice where its title verso survives.

terence-riley-comedies: The Comedies of Terence, literally translated into English prose
terence-goodluck-andrian: Terence's Andrian, a comedy in five acts
plautus-nixon-v1: Plautus, vol. 1: Amphitryo, Asinaria, Aulularia, Bacchides, Captivi

plautus-riley-comedies-v1: The Comedies of Plautus, vol. 1 (Bohn; 1913 printing)
plautus-riley-comedies-v2: The Comedies of Plautus, vol. 2 (Bohn; 1913 printing)
plautus-nixon-v3: Plautus, vol. 3: The Merchant, The Braggart Warrior, Mostellaria, The Persian (Loeb, 1924)

_excluded.Paul Nixon, Loeb Plautus (1916-38): vols. 1 (PG) and 3 (IA) held; vol. 2 (1917) no readable scan yet; vols. 4-5 first printed 1932 and 1938, not PD
